title: When Renormalisation Remembers: UV/IR Mixing as an Entanglement Bridge
abstract: Renormalisation is traditionally understood to be a Wilsonian memoryless process in which ultraviolet (UV) degrees of freedom gradually decouple, leaving an autonomous infrared (IR) description. However this need not be the case: in UV/IR mixed theories correlations between widely separated scales can persist. In this work I recast UV/IR mixing as a Hilbert-space phenomenon, realised as correlations across renormalisation scales. This formulation is implemented using the Born-Reciprocal Tensor Network (BRTN), a new configuration of tensor network that is globally symmetric under phase-space reciprocity. On this network I prepare the vacuum and reproduce the expected radiative corrections. The resulting renormalisation geometry exhibits memory, with a bridge linking reciprocal representations of IR physics, whose cross-bridge entanglement provides a precise criterion for the viability of an effective description. I analyse when this criterion is met, and show that there is a large-volume limit, with the fundamental scale held fixed, in which the obstruction to a local description scales away: Wilsonian behaviour is restored and renormalisation forgets. The BRTN therefore provides a concrete and calculable platform for UV/IR mixing.
summary: This work introduces the Born-Reciprocal Tensor Network (BRTN) as a novel computational framework to model Quantum Field Theories exhibiting UV/IR mixing. It reframes this mixing as a measurable entanglement structure across renormalization scales. The key finding is that while mixing occurs, standard local QFT behavior is recovered in the large volume limit by analyzing how this cross-bridge entanglement vanishes.
main_problem: The paper addresses UV/IR mixing in Quantum Field Theories (QFTs), where traditional scale separation assumptions fail due to residual ultraviolet structure influencing long-distance physics.
main_result: It demonstrates that the Born-Reciprocal Tensor Network (BRTN) provides a calculable platform for studying this mixing, showing that standard Wilsonian behavior is restored in the large-volume limit by analyzing cross-bridge entanglement.
method: The core method involves recasting UV/IR mixing as a Hilbert-space phenomenon and implementing it using the novel Born-Reciprocal Tensor Network (BRTN), which extends tensor network techniques to incorporate global phase-space reciprocity.
model_or_system: The model is based on QFTs, specifically analyzing scalar fields ($\phi_A$) interacting with a reciprocal background ($\phi_B$), structured within the BRTN framework. The analysis compares this structure to standard lattice QFT simulations using TTNs/TEBD.
key_observables: Cross-bridge entanglement (criterion for effective description), Effective State Entropy ($S_{	ext{eff}}$), Structure Factor $S(k)$, and momentum non-conservation amplitudes.
important_parameters: Large volume limit ($N 	o \infty$), fundamental scale ($M^*$), physical mass ($m_{	ext{phys}}$), and the coupling constant ($g$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that UV/IR mixing can be formulated as a global Hilbert-space correlation structure, which the BRTN is designed to capture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons between Wilsonian tracing (information loss) and TTN representation (global purity), and show the geometric organization of correlations in 1D QFTs using tree structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the failure of standard Wilsonian assumptions due to UV/IR mixing, introducing the BRTN as a Hilbert-space realization, demonstrating its calculational power by analyzing entanglement criteria, and finally showing how normal QFT behavior is recovered in the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: It provides a sophisticated information-theoretic lens (entanglement structure) to analyze fundamental concepts like renormalization group flow and scale separation in QFTs, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent physics in complex quantum systems.

This is a prototypical set-up for a one dimensional QFT with two scalar fields ϕA and ϕB discretized over eight space points X1...8 as the quadrature variables of the local Hilbert spaces, ϕA ≡ˆqA,n and ϕB ≡ˆqB,n respectively. Highlighted in red is the path connecting points A2 and A3 through their lowest common ancestor (LCA) at N1, which has to be traversed in order to implement the eiδt ˆqA,2 ˆqA,3 link gate. The cluster of bonds in green shows the nontrivial contractions within the entanglement wedge of the ℓ= 3 contiguous region ϕB(X5)ϕB(X6)ϕB(X7). This roughly determines how correlation lengths translate...

Figure 4: A more symmetrical version of a TTN in which every node, including the root node, carries three indices. The bulk encodes the renormalisation geometry while the physical degrees of freedom live on the boundary. In the gapped system that we consider here we do not need to impose hyperbolic tiling: if one does so then in principle the root node no longer occupies a special position.

Figure 5: Comparison of the structure factor of the QFT vacuum versus the theoretical one, for the free field with N = 128 space points, and mass m = 1 in the potential. Here we take local DVR Hilbert space of dimension 6, cut-off of 1 × 10−6 and maximum bond dimension of 20. The best fit has meff = 0.982 and C0 = −5 × 10−4.
Figure 6: Bond entropy with depth in the standard TTN, showing characteristic peaking in the centre, where the bonds are dividing the global system into roughly equally sized subsystems.

Figure 7: Born-reciprocal renormalisation geometry: the BRTN. In a genuinely Born-reciprocal theory, ϕB(Ki) is a dual field that is localised in momentum-space Ki...8, and is delocalised in position-space. The UV interface consists of pairwise links Xi ↔Ki between position- and momentum-space sites. These bonds form the entanglement bridge. Global Born-reciprocity consists of exchanging Xi ↔Ki and the fields ϕA and ϕB, flipping the entire network about the red dashed line. This line delineates the furthest into the UV that the theory can go. The upper and lower trees flow to distinct infrared roots.
